A.naturalness: “We don’t have to figure out what kind of help you want right now” is comfortable and responsive.
A.useful_understanding: “What feels most off in this moment” supplies one focused clarification.
A.grounding: “What feels most off” asks rather than inventing a concern or diagnosing a feeling.
A.user_control: “Or would you rather just sit with it together?” makes further explanation optional.

B.naturalness: “That’s okay—you don’t have to know what kind of help you want yet” responds gently to uncertainty.
B.useful_understanding: “Start with what feels most noticeable right now” provides a usable opening without demanding a defined help request.
B.grounding: “You’ve noticed that things feel off” reflects the user’s statement; “even if” frames difficulty expressing it conditionally.
B.user_control: “We can stay with that, or start with” leaves the direction and pace open.

rationale: Both meet the goal: they allow uncertainty, offer one optional opening, and neither diagnose nor prescribe an activity. A asks directly; B offers an indirect invitation. That difference does not establish a meaningful usefulness advantage, and B’s additional paraphrase receives no extra credit. Safety/privacy judgments concern observable language only; system behavior and actual emotional benefit are not established.
